---
title: "Does the 1 g static deflection change the lift-to-drag ratio?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Show code"
ALPHAS = np.array([1.0, 2.33, 3.67, 5.0])

reference = reference_point()
cl_ref, glide_speed = reference["CL"], reference["speed"]

# The 1 g airload at best glide, and the shape it bends the spar into.
loads = spanwise_load(MASS * GRAVITY / 2, speed=glide_speed, alpha=3.0)
spar = wing_spar(loads["station_y"], loads["load_per_metre"])
deflection, spar_y = np.array(spar.u), np.array(spar.y)
slope = np.gradient(deflection, spar_y)

tip_rise = float(deflection[-1])
tip_rise_fraction = tip_rise / (SPAN / 2) * 100

# The spar is inextensible, so bending up also draws the tip INBOARD: projected
# span is the arc integrated with its own slope, not the undeformed station.
# Leaving this out would let the wing gain span by bending, which is the part
# that would actually have changed the induced drag.
projected_y = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(
    np.cos(np.arctan(slope[:-1])) * np.diff(spar_y))])
span_lost = (SPAN / 2 - projected_y[-1]) * 1e3


def deflected_airplane():
    """The same aircraft with its wing moved onto the 1 g deflected shape."""
    xsecs = []
    for xsec in WING.xsecs:
        station = float(xsec.xyz_le[1])
        xsecs.append(asb.WingXSec(
            xyz_le=[float(xsec.xyz_le[0]),
                    float(np.interp(station, spar_y, projected_y)),
                    float(xsec.xyz_le[2]) + float(np.interp(station, spar_y, deflection))],
            chord=xsec.chord, twist=xsec.twist, airfoil=xsec.airfoil))
    return asb.Airplane(
        name="Discus-2c (1 g deflected)", xyz_ref=XYZ_REF,
        wings=[asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=xsecs), *AIRPLANE.wings[1:]],
        fuselages=AIRPLANE.fuselages, s_ref=WING_AREA, c_ref=MAC, b_ref=SPAN)


flexible = deflected_airplane()


def compare(build):
    """Drag at the reference CL, rigid and deflected, from the same analysis."""
    rigid_cd = drag_at_reference(lambda a: build(AIRPLANE, a), cl_ref, ALPHAS)
    flex_cd = drag_at_reference(lambda a: build(flexible, a), cl_ref, ALPHAS)
    return cl_ref / rigid_cd, cl_ref / flex_cd


def point(alpha):
    return asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=glide_speed, alpha=alpha)


results = [
    ("AeroBuildup", *compare(lambda ap, a: asb.AeroBuildup(
        airplane=ap, op_point=point(a), xyz_ref=XYZ_REF).run())),
    ("LiftingLine", *compare(lambda ap, a: asb.LiftingLine(
        airplane=ap, op_point=point(a), xyz_ref=XYZ_REF,
        spanwise_resolution=8).run())),
]

worst = max(abs(flex - rigid) / rigid * 100 for _, rigid, flex in results)
hero = next(r for r in results if r[0] == "LiftingLine")

# Deflecting a wing cannot reduce its induced drag at fixed lift, so a gain here
# would mean the geometry was rebuilt wrong rather than that flexibility helps.
assert all(flex <= rigid + 1e-9 for _, rigid, flex in results), \
    "deflection improved L/D; the deflected geometry is suspect"
```

::: {.hero-pair}
::: {}
[`{python} f"{hero[1]:.2f}"`]{.hero-value}
[rigid wing]{.hero-label}
:::
::: {}
[`{python} f"{hero[2]:.2f}"`]{.hero-value .hero-ref}
[on the 1 g deflected shape]{.hero-label}
:::
:::

**Answer.** No. At 1 g the tip rises [`{python} f"{tip_rise:.3f}"`]{.key} m,
`{python} f"{tip_rise_fraction:.1f}"`% of semi-span, and the inextensible spar
draws it inboard by only [`{python} f"{span_lost:.1f}"`]{.key} mm — so projected
span barely moves. Glide ratio falls by at most
[`{python} f"{worst:.2f}"`]{.key}% (@tbl-deflection), a twentieth of a glide
point. That is far below the disagreement between aerodynamic
methods, so flexibility is not what limits confidence here.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Bending only — there is no torsion

The spar carries bending stiffness only, so aeroelastic washout — the static
effect that redistributes span loading — cannot appear.
:::

```{python}
#| label: tbl-deflection
#| tbl-cap: "Glide ratio at the reference lift coefficient on the rigid geometry and on the 1 g deflected shape, for the two viscous methods available in-process."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
md_table(
    ["", "rigid", "deflected", "change"],
    [[name, f"{rigid:.2f}", f"{flex:.2f}", f"{(flex - rigid) / rigid * 100:+.2f}%"]
     for name, rigid, flex in results],
)
```
